content.summary: Guidance on implementation of ESC 0 h/1 h and 0 h/2 h algorithms for suspected myocardial infarction (MI) with focus on use of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays and complementary diagnostic steps.
key_points: The ESC 0 h/1 h and 0 h/2 h algorithms must be integrated with a detailed clinical assessment and a 12-lead ECG.
Repeat blood sampling is mandatory when there is ongoing or recurrent chest pain.

Artificial intelligence models that include serial hs-cTn measurements and individual risk profiles have been proposed to facilitate personalized diagnostic evaluation and prediction of MI events during the first 30 days.
Cut-off levels for the 0 h/1 h and 0 h/2 h algorithms are assay-specific; assay-specific cut-offs are provided in Supplementary data (Table S4).

Practical guidance: to maximize safety and feasibility, blood samples for hs-cTn at 0 h and 1 h should be obtained irrespective of other clinical details and pending results. The 0 h sample should be obtained immediately after admission to the ED.

Obtaining routine 0 h/1 h sampling may lead to unnecessary cTn measurements in approximately 10–15% of patients with very low 0 h concentrations and chest pain onset >3 h, but this practice facilitates the diagnostic process and increases patient safety.

Other biomarkers: use of biomarkers other than cTn for ACS diagnosis is not recommended unless cTn is unavailable. Among additional biomarkers evaluated for NSTEMI, creatine kinase myocardial band (CK-MB), myosin-binding protein C, and copeptin may have some clinical relevance when used in combination with standard cTn T/I, but their incremental value above cTn is limited in most clinical situations.

Non-invasive imaging: transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) performed/interpreted by trained healthcare professionals should be routinely available in emergency rooms and chest pain units and can help identify signs suggestive of ongoing ischemia when ACS diagnostic uncertainty exists.

practical_recommendations.sampling_timing: Obtain hs-cTn at 0 h and 1 h for the 0 h/1 h algorithm irrespective of other clinical details; 0 h sample immediately after ED admission.
practical_recommendations.repeat_sampling: Mandatory when ongoing or recurrent chest pain; repeat measurements as clinically indicated.
practical_recommendations.assay_specific_cutoffs: Use assay-specific cut-offs (refer to Supplementary data Table S4).
practical_recommendations.use_of_other_biomarkers: Not recommended as a routine replacement for cTn; CK-MB, myosin-binding protein C, and copeptin may be adjuncts but add limited incremental value.

content.limitations_noted: Incremental diagnostic value of additional biomarkers above and beyond cTn is limited in most clinical situations.
